result.topic_en: Solution of the Pothenot (resection) problem reduced to three equations, rewritten symmetrically with the substitution aα+bβ+cγ=ω, and a parametrisation with complex numbers whose arguments correspond to the observed azimuths, plus a sign condition for physical possibility.
result.transcription:
Die Auflösung der Pothenotschen Aufgabe beruhet auf den
drei Gleichungen
$\frac{\alpha a+\beta b+\gamma c}{\alpha}\cdot x' - \frac{\alpha' a'+\beta' b'+\gamma' c'}{\alpha'}\cdot x - \frac{\alpha a+\beta b+\gamma c}{\alpha}\cdot a' + \frac{\beta' b'+\gamma' c'}{\alpha'}\cdot a = 0$
$\frac{\alpha a+\beta b+\gamma c}{\beta}\, x' - \frac{\alpha' a'+\gamma' c'}{\beta'}\, x - \frac{\alpha a+\gamma c}{\beta}\cdot b' + \frac{\alpha' a'+\gamma' c'}{\beta'}\cdot b = 0$
$\frac{\alpha a+\beta b+\gamma c}{\gamma}\, x' - \frac{\alpha' a'+\beta' b'}{\gamma'}\cdot x - \frac{\alpha a+\beta b}{\gamma}\cdot c' + \frac{\alpha' a'+\beta' b'}{\gamma'}\cdot c = 0$
wovon jede schon in den beiden andern erhalten [-seyn[?]-] ist
Also $a\alpha+b\beta+c\gamma=\omega$ gesetzt
[-$\left(\frac{\beta}{\beta'}-\frac{\gamma}{\gamma'}\right)\omega' x + \left(\frac{\beta b'}{\beta'}-\frac{\gamma c'}{\gamma'}\right)\omega +$-] $\beta b$
$\left(\frac{\beta}{\beta'}-\frac{\gamma}{\gamma'}\right)\omega' x + (b'-c')\omega - \left(\frac{\beta b}{\beta'}-\frac{\gamma c}{\gamma'}\right)\omega' = 0$
$\left(\frac{\gamma}{\gamma'}-\frac{\alpha}{\alpha'}\right)\omega' x + (c'-a')\omega - \left(\frac{\gamma c}{\gamma'}-\frac{\alpha a}{\alpha'}\right)\omega' = 0$
$\left(\frac{\alpha}{\alpha'}-\frac{\beta}{\beta'}\right)\omega' x + (a'-b')\omega - \left(\frac{\alpha a}{\alpha'}-\frac{\beta b}{\beta'}\right)\omega' = 0$
Noch zierlicher
$(\alpha\beta'-\beta\alpha')(\alpha' a'+\beta' b'+\gamma' c')\, x + \alpha a\beta'\gamma'(b'-c') + \beta b\alpha'\gamma'(c'-a')$
$+ \gamma c\beta'\alpha'(a'-b')$
$=0$
[-Die Bedingung-]
Sind A. B. C drei complexe Zahlen deren Winkel den beobachteten
Azimuthen entsprechen, so kann man setzen
$\alpha = A(BC'-CB')$
$\beta = B(CA'-AC')$
$\gamma = C(AB'-BA')$
Die [-Möglichkeit-] physische Möglichkeit beruhet darauf daß
$B'C(A-B)(A'-C') - BC'(A'-B')(A-C)$
mit den beiden andern symmetrisch daraus folgenden Grossen einerlei Zeichen haben
